weakest_line: Some Christians also wonder about this question sometimes.
one_fix: Answer the 'forever' half of the hook head-on with one strong text instead of four signposted points made of familiar verses, and cut the 'enemy wants you lost' preaching.

weakest_line: Even when he demanded a Philistine wife, his parents "did not know that it was from the LORD, for he was seeking an opportunity against the Philistines."
one_fix: Cut the Philistine-wife detour and state the 'oh' plainly: his strength was equipment for a job, not a grade on his life. Then build the reveal around 'he did not know the LORD had left him.'
Open on the concrete puzzle, 'If God knew where Adam was, why did He ask "Where art thou?"', instead of a sermon aimed at 'you', and end with a question for viewers in place of the exhortation.

weakest_line: It's one of the most asked questions about the Bible and most Christians can't answer it.
one_fix: Replace the flat 'you'll know what to say' close with a real prompt for responses, and lead the payoff with the less-known clue (Genesis 5:4 'sons and daughters' plus Abraham and Sarah) before the familiar 'he married a sister' answer.

weakest_line: So God gave us free will, and He tells us plainly which way to choose.
one_fix: Ground the answer in Genesis 2-3 itself (for example, the tree of life also stood in the garden and was freely given) rather than a hypothetical about removing every temptation.

weakest_line: Work in that world would feel like tending something you love.
one_fix: Tie each speculative 'world without the fall' claim to a specific verse, and drop the assumption that every viewer prays.

weakest_line: Because it was the only thing standing between a family and death.
one_fix: Actually answer 'why blood' from Exodus 12 (the lamb dies in the firstborn's place; 'when I see the blood, I will pass over you') in place of the Exodus recap and the circular answer.

weakest_line: So, let's allow the Bible to answer it.
one_fix: Collapse the three-answer structure into one strong through-line built on Cornelius, cut the signposting, and end with a question for viewers rather than assuming someone told them about Jesus.

weakest_line: And if you're here to stand for God's word, welcome to the Valiant.
one_fix: Open on the golden-calf paradox (they saw the sea split and still made an idol within weeks) and trim the stack of philosopher names so it plays on one listen.
Cut the colleague-lies-about-you analogy and go straight from 'knowing is not causing' to the Peter and Judas contrast.
